title: Finite reduced normalization: coherent quotient and local normality criterion
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Assume that $
u$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $C_X=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_X	o
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})$ be the normalization cokernel [def-trf-conductor-cokernel]. There is a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X\longrightarrow
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}\longrightarrow C_X\longrightarrow0,$$
and both $
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}$ and $C_X$ are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, put $B=\Gamma(
u^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_{X^
u})$. The structure map identifies $A$ with a subring of $B$, and $C_X|_U$ is canonically the quasi-coherent module associated to the finite $A$-module $B/A$. For $x\in X$ put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and let $\overline R$ be the integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] of $R$ in its total ring of fractions, the localization obtained by inverting all non-zero-divisors. Canonically, as $R$-modules,
$$C_{X,x}\cong\overline R/R,$$
with the numerator identified with $(
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})_x$. In particular, $C_{X,x}=0$ if and only if $R$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

proof.text: Every quasi-compact open of $X$ is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, hence has finitely many irreducible components by lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components. Apply lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions on each affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$: $B=\overline A\subseteq Q(A)$ with structural map $a\mapsto a/1$. This map is injective: $a/1=0$ means $ta=0$ for a non-zero-divisor $t$, hence $a=0$. Thus the sheaf map is injective on all affine opens, and on any open its kernel is zero by restriction to an affine open covering and the sheaf uniqueness axiom. The definition of the normalization cokernel now gives the claimed short exact sequence. The finite-morphism definition also gives that $B$ is a finite $A$-module. On the empty affine open all these rings and modules are zero.

source.place: Tag 035P, lemma-description-normalization; finite morphism definition, with the elementary injectivity and sheaf argument written out

proof.text:
By def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, finiteness of $
u$ says that $
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}$ is a quasi-coherent finite type $\mathcal O_X$-module. It is coherent by pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth, since $X$ is locally Noetherian. The same lemma makes $\mathcal O_X$ coherent: on every affine chart it is $\widetilde A$ and is generated by $1$. Apply the coherent-cokernel clause of lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum to their structural map. Its cokernel is precisely $C_X$, so $C_X$ is coherent as asserted.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image to the structural map (its two modules are quasi-coherent by the previous step). On each affine $U$ it gives $C_X(U)=B/A$, with the canonical quotient map. Images of a finite set of $A$-generators of $B$ generate $B/A$. To identify the sheaf, apply lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-basic-open-localization to $C_X$: on $D(f)\subset U$ its two clauses say exactly that restriction induces $(B/A)_f\simeq C_X(D(f))$ (send $m/f^r$ to $f^{-r}m|_{D(f)}$; surjectivity is clause (1), and its kernel is zero by clause (2)). These identifications commute with restrictions because they are given by restriction of the same sections and multiplication by inverse powers of $f$. By lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections they identify $C_X|_U$ with $\widetilde{B/A}$ on the principal-open basis; the compatible basis isomorphisms glue uniquely by the sheaf axiom. This proves the canonical affine quotient assertion.

source.place: Tag 01IC, lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent; the principal-open localization description of quasi-coherent modules

proof.text:
Fix $x\in U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, corresponding to $\mathfrak p$, and put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$. The affine ring $A$ is Noetherian by pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth and reduced by def-pc-reduced-scheme. Identify $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}=A_{\mathfrak p}$ by lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization. Finiteness of $
u$ implies affineness by definition, so lem-sc-affine-pushforward-stalk-localization identifies $(
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})_x$ with $S^{-1}B$, using its structural map from $R$. Step 1 identified $B$ as the integral closure of $A$ in $Q(A)$. Lemma lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization therefore identifies $S^{-1}B$ with the integral closure of $R$ in $S^{-1}Q(A)$. Apply lem-trf-total-fractions-prime-localization to identify this ambient ring canonically with $Q(R)$ over $R$. Thus the numerator is exactly $\overline R$, with its structural inclusion of $R$; the identifications are as $R$-algebras, hence also as $R$-modules.

source.place: Tag 0C3B, lemma-stalk-normalization, localization proof; algebra.tex Tag 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize

proof.text: By lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact (3), the stalk of the cokernel is the quotient of the target stalk by the image of the source stalk. Step 4 identifies that inclusion with $R\hookrightarrow\overline R$, giving canonically $C_{X,x}\cong\overline R/R$. The ring $R$ is reduced by def-pc-reduced-scheme and Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian applied to the affine ring of step 4; it has finitely many minimal primes by lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes. The quotient vanishes precisely when $R$ is integrally closed in $Q(R)$, hence precisely when $R$ is a normal ring by lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions. A normal local ring is a normal domain: its localization at its maximal ideal is itself (all denominators are units), and the definition of a normal ring applies at that prime. Conversely an integrally closed domain has $\overline R=R$ directly, since its total ring of fractions is its fraction field. This proves both directions of the stated criterion; the stalk assertions are vacuous for empty $X$.

The item's statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint match the live copy: this is the first split, nothing is weakened, there is no cycle and no SGA citation. Step 1: open subschemes are locally Noetherian and quasi-compact ones have finitely many components, which is the hypothesis of lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions. That gives B = integral closure of A in Q(A); a ↦ a/1 is injective and the kernel sheaf vanishes on an affine basis. Step 2: finite gives ν_*O quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent by 01XZ; O_X is coherent; clause (1) of kernel-cokernel-sum makes the cokernel coherent. Step 3: clauses (2) and (3) of quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image, the two clauses of the basic-open localization lemma and tilde sections give C_X|_U = tilde(B/A). Step 4: R = A_p, (ν_*O)_x = S^{-1}B, integral closure commutes with localization, and the new node identifies S^{-1}Q(A) with Q(R) over R. Step 5: clause (3) of module-stalk-exact gives C_{X,x} = R̄/R. R is reduced, Noetherian and has finitely many minimal primes, so reduced-normal-iff applies; local normal means R_m = R is a domain, and a domain has Q = Frac. New node lem-trf-total-fractions-prime-localization is true: Q(A) = ∏ A_q, S^{-1} keeps exactly the q ⊆ p, and those are the minimal primes of A_p. I tested it on k×k with p = 0×k (S contains a zero-divisor) and on k[x,y]/(xy) at (x). It is self-contained and statement-only, sourced to 02LX as an agent consequence; Mathlib's isFractionRing_of_isLocalization needs S inside the non-zero-divisors, so it is not a leaf. It duplicates none of reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions, totalquotient-minimal-product, total-fraction-fiber-decomposition, flat-birational-normalization-comparison or normalization-affine-stalk-closure (the last only over a field of finite type), and restates no clause of the item.
